summary.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a recovery-led quarter: total recoveries rose 151% to INR1,066 crores and standalone PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores, driven by a large corporate resolution. Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: About 68% of AUM and a corporate book of about INR13,000 crores; recoveries are chunky and event-driven, which drove the Q1 spike.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: About 24% of AUM; over 3.29 million retail borrowers on the platform, with steady granular repayments. Retail and SME rose from about 21% to 31% of AUM since March 2024.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: About 8% of AUM; management treats SME as an independent business it wants to grow.

segments.name: Collection as a service
segments.commentary: Still at infrastructure-build and proof-of-concept stage with own assets and a few NBFCs; no revenue or pipeline numbers given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical AUM or acquisition guidance; management expects AUM to rise while acquisitions are matched by equal resolutions, with resolutions of about 20-25% of opening AUM each year.
Management expects acquisitions to rise through Q2 and Q3, with pipelines described as strong, and to draw down more borrowings and marginally increase leverage.
Write-backs of previously written-off assets are expected to decline over time; maximum write-offs over the next three years are cumulatively under INR100 crores.
Management expects its fee income momentum to be maintained, though it said the Q1 write-back was not a full-year trend.
capex_capacity: Borrowings were reduced to INR1,100 crores in Q1 to fund acquisitions later in the year; cash and bank balances INR252 crores, which management says gives ample capacity to fund acquisitions.

Own investment in AUM was about INR4,200 crores (about 22% of AUM) as of June; the FY26 average investment ratio was about 33% (INR2,000 crores on INR6,000 crores acquired), and Q1 FY27 is running at about 40%.
Mandatory minimum SR investment is 15%; co-investor deals allow as low as 2.5%.
Last-mile funding of up to 25% of acquired loan value is available to support turnarounds.
demand_pricing: Industry stress (banks and NBFCs, including SMA, NPA and written-off) is about INR23 lakh crores per management, growing about INR1 lakh crore a year; ARCs participate in roughly 10%.
Special mention accounts were about 30% of new ARC acquisitions in FY25, up from about 14% in FY24 (CRISIL data cited by management).
Acquisition cost held at 26-27% of dues every year; Arcil's AUM is about 14% of the INR1.4 lakh crore dues under management.
Arcil's share of industry AUM rose from 11% to 15% over two years; share of new acquisitions was 17% in FY26 on about INR6,000 crores acquired.
Management attributed improved industry recovery rates (cited as moving from about 35% to about 85%) to a stronger economy and real estate recovery.
